documents.title: AI & Academic Integrity - Artificial Intelligence & Information Literacy
documents.summary: A short university library guide page giving three tips: ask instructors about their AI policies, treat AI as a source not a substitute, and cite AI tools. It says AI use without permission or citation can be plagiarism or a code of conduct violation. It sets no university-wide rule itself.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule on whether AI is allowed; it says AI use "without permission" is a violation and tells students to "Ask instructors about their AI use policies", which leaves the decision to instructors, so delegates.

units.why: "VSU upholds academic honesty" states the institution's value as the reason for the AI rules that follow; it is a statement of fact (informs) addressed to everyone, and grounds the rule in honesty rather than skill-building, so P95 rather than P41.

"Using AI without permission or proper citation can lead to plagiarism or code of conduct violations" classifies unauthorized or uncited AI use as plagiarism/conduct violation, so P36; it also implies a permission and citation requirement, but the classification is the stated point.
units.anchor: AI without permission or proper citation can lead to plagiarism or code of conduct violations.
units.fit_note: Also implies AI requires permission and citation, which the type does not capture.

units.why: "Ask instructors about their AI use policies" directs students to check with instructors, a recommendation ("Tips"), so should; P10 (ask before using) fits as the nearest type.
units.anchor: Ask instructors about their AI use policies
units.fit_note: Asks about instructors' policies in general, not specifically when unsure.

units.why: "Treat AI like a source, not a substitute" tells students AI must not replace their own work; closest to P32 (AI must not replace thinking). It also treats AI as a source, but a source to be cited, not a collaborator, so P45/P96 fit less well.
units.anchor: Treat AI like a source , not a substitute
units.fit_note: Frames AI as a source (cited) rather than a substitute, which goes beyond problem-solver framing.

units.why: "Cite AI tools using your class's citation style (APA, MLA, etc.)" tells students to cite AI use in a named style, a recommended disclosure practice, so P24.
units.anchor: Cite AI tools using your class’s citation style (APA, MLA, etc.)

units.why: "tools like Grammarly, ChatGPT, or Quillbot are aids, not authors" states that AI tools are not authors, matching P96 (AI is neither author nor source); it is framed as a reminder (informs).
units.anchor: tools like Grammarly, ChatGPT, or Quillbot are aids, not authors.
units.fit_note: Also names Grammarly and Quillbot as aids, implying writing-support tools are acceptable aids.

notes: Only one thin library-guide document included; no computing or school documents exist. Topic codes taken from tools/AGENT_BRIEF.md.
